title: Prove the semantic document reader convergence
summary: Build one reversible x-plus-3 walking skeleton that combines KP's typed semantic animation kernel, URL/provenance/provider boundaries, and inferred authoring with document-first static delivery, continuous learner-controlled scroll sampling, a lightweight equation DOM adapter, shared focus, and a mandatory human visual-review stop before generalization.

sourceRefs.summary: Approved evidence, target architecture, asset parity, budgets, migration order, and exemplar gate.
Current semantic-animation and concept-room strategy that the convergence action must preserve.
Current semantic animation asset and transformation-composition contract to preserve.
Renderer-neutral Time-to-Frame sampling spine for all reader clocks.
Current discrete story clock whose learner behavior the new reader clock must replace without destabilizing other routes.
Current persistent semantic material-owner technique to retain and simplify in the reader adapter.
Current compiler-to-editor coupling seam the walking skeleton must replace.

progress.summary: The 30-slice semantic reader convergence implementation and automated review package are complete. The route is static-first, continuously reversible, linkable, accessible, isolated, and under provisional budgets. Human visual acceptance is now mandatory; cancellation collision, late solution-glyph handoff, salience breadth, and mobile whitespace are explicitly unresolved.

expectedLearning: Whether a compact document compiler and lightweight reader can expose the existing semantic kernel with legacy-quality continuous symbolic motion and dramatically lower learner-route cost.
Whether one renderer-neutral clock, focus, URL, and hydration contract is sufficient for later SVG, code, graph, provider, and WebGL exemplars without generalizing them now.
allowedWork: Characterize and preserve the current x-plus-3 semantics, URL/provenance/provider contracts, and legacy motion behavior.
Add the minimum LessonDocument, static compiler, reader clock/URL/focus/hydration seams, and equation DOM adapter needed for one isolated x-plus-3 route.

Adapt continuous scroll progress, actual KaTeX measurement, perceptual anchor alignment, persistent material owners, lazy hydration, static HTML, and deterministic verification behind current semantic interfaces.
Add focused architecture, compiler, runtime, browser, accessibility, performance, route-closure, and visual evidence; commit each verified slice independently.
disallowedWork: Do not port the legacy parser, focus-widget runtime, code-projection runtime, page CSS system, or legacy repository wholesale.

Do not change the general semantic asset model, editor player, unrelated routes, FTC, economics, programming, graph, diagram, provider, or WebGL implementations except for narrow compatibility seams proven necessary by the exemplar.
Do not promote exemplar-local styles, clocks, focus behavior, Markdown vocabulary, budgets, or renderer APIs across families before explicit human visual acceptance.
Do not import editor or Three.js code into the learner route, require JavaScript for reading, update URLs on every scroll frame, or parse HTML during ordinary animation frames.
